subject: Aurora AI — sizing ask & flexible term/pricing scenarios
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Chen <lucas@aurora.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@aurora.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora sizing baseline + term options (attached)

Lucas — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a baseline capacity sheet with the conservative QPS / concurrency profile you shared (aurora_capacity_baseline_v2.xlsx).

What I need from you to put a formal reserved capacity proposal together:
- Confirmation that the baseline concurrency/peak windows reflect the production traffic (rows highlighted yellow).
- A preferred commit tenor: 12 / 18 / 24 / 36 months (you can pick a primary and a fallback).
- Any contractual constraints from procurement (billing cadence, PO or invoice, SOW requirements).

High-level notes so you have context: our pricing sensitivity to GPU market cost looks like this — longer tenors let us pass larger discounts on unit GPU-hour costs, but discounts above ~20% need finance approval and an updated reserved SKU mix. If you want, I can run three pricing scenarios (conservative, mid, aggressive) across A100/H100 mixes and show the impact on per-token cost and committed spend.

If you can confirm the above by Wednesday EOD I’ll share the scenarios + a draft term sheet for legal.

Thanks,
— Priyom
Priyom Das | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom.d@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

> Priyom / Karthik — see attached draft scenarios (redwood_pricing_scenarios.pdf). Summary below so it’s easy to forward: 
>
> Scenario A — Conservative (12 mo)
> - Hardware: Mixed A100 (70%) / H100 (30%)
> - Committed hours: 9,600 GPU-hours/month
> - Effective discount vs on-demand: ~12%
> - Finance approval: not required (<= 15%)
> - Overages: billed at on-demand + 10% surcharge or use burst credits (recommended for initial canary)
>
> Scenario B — Baseline (24 mo)
> - Hardware: Mixed A100/H100 50/50
> - Committed hours: 11,200 GPU-hours/month
> - Effective discount vs on-demand: ~18%
> - Finance approval: required for discounts >= 18% — pre-approved band exists for 15-20% with regional finance signoff
> - Price-pass: annual true-up clause available; any sustained market GPU cost reductions >8% can trigger a partial pass-through adjustment at anniversary (requires legal addendum)
>
> Scenario C — Aggressive (36 mo)
> - Hardware: H100-heavy (65%) with some A100 for batch jobs
> - Committed hours: 13,500 GPU-hours/month
> - Effective discount vs on-demand: ~24%
> - Finance approval: required (discount >20%). Escalation path: Marissa (Finance) -> CFO sign-off for >25% deviations.
> - Price-pass: possible structured credit if GPU market falls more than 12% across a 12-month lookback; negotiation required on exact mechanics.
>
> Operational notes:
> - We recommend delivering a 3-month canary on Scenario B with burst credit controls; if Aurora's traffic matches the baseline we convert the remaining months.
> - To keep latency SLOs, schedule H100-backed pools for the 8am-8pm PST peak.
>
> Next steps: Priyom, can you confirm which scenario(s) Aurora wants in the draft term sheet and I’ll flag Marissa for formal finance approval if they pick Scenario C?\>
>
> Neha

> Priyom / Team — thanks for the scenarios and the clear approval path. After internal review we want to proceed with the following: 
>
> - Start: Scenario B (24 mo) as the baseline commit, but with a 3-month canary (first 3 months at 50% of committed hours then scale to full consumption if canary metrics look good).
> - Hardware: begin with mixed A100/H100 50/50; reserve the option to shift to H100-heavier after Q2 2028.
> - Pricing: agree to the annual true-up clause (partial pass-through) for market GPU cost reductions >8% at each anniversary.
> - Contract: procurement will sign a 12-month binding term for the canary and a 24-month master commitment (DocuSign link preferred). Please attach the draft term sheet and send over the DocuSign.
>
